content: Hospitals should be arranged like night clubs: places where people go to celebrate life and heal with joy, rather than grim temples of fear.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

Across his life and work, Alan Watts saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
